summary: Robert P. Scharlemann worked in religious studies and philosophy after studying at Concordia College, Concordia Seminary, and Heidelberg University. He held posts at the University of Southern California (~1966–1968), University of Iowa (~1968–1981), and University of Virginia (~1981–2004).

Robert S. Ellwood was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Colorado, Yale University, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, later serving on the faculty at the University of Southern California (~1967–1997).

Robert S. Nelson is an art historian who studied at Rice University and New York University. He served as Professor at the University of Chicago (~1977–2005) before taking up a post at Yale University in ~2005.
Robert S. P. Beekes was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leiden University under F. B. J. Kuiper. He held posts at Marnix Gymnasium and Leiden University (1973, 1979).
Robert Sewell was an Indologist and historian who served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1894) and was Keeper at the Tamil Nadu Archives.

Robert Seymour Conway was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at the City of London School. He held academic posts at Newnham College (~1888–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).
Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Karen C. Lang and K. L. Seshagiri Rao (attested 1994).

Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St Beuno's and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as Professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and led the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Robert Zydenbos is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Utrecht University. He has held positions at the University of Munich (~2001), the University of Toronto, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).
Robert van Gulik was a sinologist and scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1929–1934) and completed his doctorate at Utrecht University (~1934–1935) under Jan Gonda.

Robin Coningham is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at King's College, Cambridge, and completed his PhD under Frank Raymond Allchin. He held professorships at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (from 2005).
Robin D. S. Yates is a historian and sinologist who completed his PhD at Harvard University (~1975–1980). He later held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University (~2005).
Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College School, Magdalen College, and completed his doctorate under John Hurrell Crook. He held a post at University College London (~1987–1994).

Philosopher Roderick M. Chisholm studied at Brown and Harvard. He held posts at the Barnes Foundation (~1946), the University of Graz, the University of Massachusetts Amherst, and served as Professor at Brown University (~1947–1987).
Roderick S. Bucknell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who served at the University of Queensland (~1976–2002), where he was an Associate Professor from ~1990 to 2002.

Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history who held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London (attested 2011 as Professor Emeritus).
Roger Brown was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Michigan (~1945–1952) and held a post at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.

Roger Caillois was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École Normale Supérieure, and under Marcel Mauss at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held a post at the United Nations (~1948–1971).
Roger Heim studied at École Centrale Paris and the Science Faculty of Paris. He was affiliated with the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle (~1929–1970), serving as its director from ~1950 to 1965.

Roger R. Jackson studied at Wesleyan and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he held a faculty post at Carleton College (~1989–2016).
